items.stem: Crowding out occurs when
options: increased government borrowing raises interest rates and reduces private sector investment
items.answer: increased government borrowing raises interest rates and reduces private sector investment
items.markingKey: Financial crowding out; also resource crowding out near full capacity.

items.stem: Explain two reasons why fiscal policy may be ineffective in reducing unemployment.
items.answer: Time lags mean the stimulus arrives too late; crowding out reduces private investment; a small multiplier (high MPM, saving); Ricardian equivalence; unemployment may be structural.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Distinguish between a cyclical and a structural budget deficit.
items.answer: Cyclical: due to the downturn (lower tax revenue, higher benefits) and disappears with recovery; structural: spending exceeds revenue even at full employment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: In Dravonia, government spending is $450 billion, tax revenue $420 billion and GDP $2000 billion. Calculate the budget deficit as a percentage of GDP.

The government of Zentara increases spending by $50 billion, financed by borrowing. The multiplier is 1.5. Higher interest rates cause private investment to fall by 25% of the extra government spending. Calculate the change in national income (a) ignoring crowding out and (b) allowing for it. Explain why crowding out may be smaller in a deep recession.
items.answer: (a) $75 billion (b) net injection = 50 − 12.5 = 37.5; ΔY = $56.2 billion. In a deep recession, private investment demand is weak and interest rates are low, so borrowing does not push rates up much.
items.markingKey: (a) 50 × 1.5 [1]; (b) net injection × k [2]; explanation: spare saving/low rates/weak investment [2].

items.stem: The government of Fendaria increases spending by $30 billion, financed by borrowing. The multiplier is 1.5. Higher interest rates cause private investment to fall by 25% of the extra government spending. Calculate the change in national income (a) ignoring crowding out and (b) allowing for it. Explain why crowding out may be smaller in a deep recession.
items.answer: (a) $45 billion (b) net injection = 30 − 7.5 = 22.5; ΔY = $33.8 billion. In a deep recession, private investment demand is weak and interest rates are low, so borrowing does not push rates up much.
items.markingKey: (a) 30 × 1.5 [1]; (b) net injection × k [2]; explanation: spare saving/low rates/weak investment [2].

items.stem: Extract: In Esteria, unemployment is 4.0%, inflation 6.5%, public debt 60% of GDP and the central bank policy rate 4.0%. Productivity growth has been below 1% a year for a decade. (a) Calculate the real policy interest rate. (b) Explain how monetary policy could be used and one limitation.
items.answer: (a) -2.5% (b) Raise rates to reduce inflation; lags and effect on growth.

items.stem: Extract: In Istrana, unemployment is 8.5%, inflation 1.0%, public debt 95% of GDP and the central bank policy rate 0.5%. Productivity growth has been below 1% a year for a decade. (a) Explain one limitation of fiscal policy in this economy. (b) Explain how monetary policy could be used and one limitation.
items.answer: (a) High debt limits borrowing; crowding out; time lags. (b) Rates near zero: limited room; QE as alternative.

items.stem: Automatic stabilisers are
options: changes in tax rates announced in the budget
features of the tax and benefit system that change automatically to dampen the business cycle
decisions made by the central bank
items.answer: features of the tax and benefit system that change automatically to dampen the business cycle
items.markingKey: E.g. progressive taxes and unemployment benefits.

items.stem: In Tarvia, government spending is $450 billion, tax revenue $420 billion and GDP $2500 billion. Calculate the budget deficit as a percentage of GDP.
Esteria has entered a recession while interest rates are already close to zero. ‘Fiscal policy is more effective than monetary policy in ending a recession.’ Evaluate this statement.
items.answer: Arguments for: Direct impact on AD, works when rates are near zero, targeted. Arguments against / evaluation: Time lags, crowding out, debt constraints, multiplier uncertainty; monetary policy faster to change; depends on situation. Conclusion: a supported judgement that depends on the conditions identified.
items.markingKey: Knowledge and analysis (about 60%): accurate theory, logical chains of reasoning and a relevant diagram described with axes, curves and shifts. Evaluation (about 40%): considers both sides, the assumptions and the context, and reaches a justified conclusion.

items.stem: The real interest rate is approximately
options: the interest rate on government bonds
the base rate set by the central bank
the nominal interest rate minus the rate of inflation
items.answer: the nominal interest rate minus the rate of inflation
items.markingKey: Fisher: r ≈ i − π.

items.stem: Explain how a rise in interest rates reduces inflation.
items.answer: Higher borrowing costs and returns to saving reduce consumption and investment; mortgage payments rise; the currency appreciates, lowering import prices and reducing net exports; AD falls and inflationary pressure eases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each channel up to 3 [3]

items.stem: Explain two limitations of monetary policy.
items.answer: Time lags of 18–24 months; zero lower bound; banks may not pass on rate cuts; low confidence; cost-push inflation not addressed; exchange rate effects in open economies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: The nominal interest rate in Korvia is 2% and inflation is 2%. Calculate the approximate real interest rate.
items.markingKey: r ≈ i − π = 2 − 2 = 0% (exactly 0%).

items.stem: In Westaria, the central bank raises the policy rate by 1.5 percentage points from 3%; inflation is 2%. A household has a $200,000 interest-only variable-rate mortgage and an income of $40,000 a year. Calculate the change in annual interest payments, the new real interest rate (approximately) and the change as a percentage of household income. Explain how this helps to reduce inflation and one reason why the effect might be weak.
items.answer: Interest rises by $3000 a year (7.5% of income); real rate ≈ 2.5%. Less disposable income reduces consumption and AD. Weak if most mortgages are fixed-rate, if households save less instead of spending less, or if inflation is cost-push.
items.markingKey: 200,000 × 1.5% [1]; real rate [1]; % of income [1]; AD channel [1]; limitation [1].

items.stem: (a) Explain the transmission mechanism of monetary policy. (b) ‘Monetary policy is the most effective way to control inflation.’ Evaluate this statement.
items.answer: (a) Explanation of the theory (with a described diagram where relevant), drawing on: Independent central bank, flexible, affects expectations. (b) Case for the view: Independent central bank, flexible, affects expectations. Case against / evaluation: Cost-push inflation, time lags, harms growth and exporters, exchange rate effects; supply-side and fiscal policies also needed. Conclusion: a judgement on the conditions under which the view holds.
items.markingKey: (a) Knowledge and understanding of the theory, clear analytical chain; diagram described accurately with labelled axes and curves. (b) Analysis of arguments for and against; evaluation reaches a justified conclusion that weighs the conditions under which the claim holds. Top level needs a judgement, not just a summary.

items.stem: Most mortgages in Dravonia are on fixed rates for five years. Explain how this affects the impact of an interest rate rise.
items.answer: Few households face higher payments quickly, so the cash-flow effect on consumption is delayed and weaker, lengthening the time lag of monetary policy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: fixed payments; 1 mark: weaker/delayed effect [2]

items.stem: In Dravonia, the central bank raises the policy rate by 2 percentage points from 5%; inflation is 3%. A household has a $150,000 interest-only variable-rate mortgage and an income of $30,000 a year. Calculate the change in annual interest payments, the new real interest rate (approximately) and the change as a percentage of household income. Explain how this helps to reduce inflation and one reason why the effect might be weak.
items.answer: Interest rises by $3000 a year (10% of income); real rate ≈ 4%. Less disposable income reduces consumption and AD. Weak if most mortgages are fixed-rate, if households save less instead of spending less, or if inflation is cost-push.
items.markingKey: 150,000 × 2% [1]; real rate [1]; % of income [1]; AD channel [1]; limitation [1].

items.stem: Which is a market-based supply-side policy?
options: Reducing the power of trade unions
items.answer: Reducing the power of trade unions
items.markingKey: Market-based: deregulation, privatisation, tax cuts, labour market reform. Interventionist: education, training, infrastructure, R&D subsidies.

items.stem: With the aid of a diagram, explain how successful supply-side policies can reduce both inflation and unemployment.
items.answer: AD/AS diagram: LRAS (or Keynesian AS) shifts right; with AD unchanged the price level falls (or rises less) and real output rises, reducing unemployment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: LRAS shift; 1 mark: lower price level; 1 mark: higher output and employment [3]

items.stem: Explain why supply-side policies may increase inequality.
items.answer: Tax cuts for higher earners, weaker unions and benefit cuts may raise incomes at the top while reducing them for the low paid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: policy; 1 mark: distributional effect [2]

items.stem: Productivity growth in Westaria rises from 2% to 3% a year after a training programme. Using the rule of 70, calculate how many fewer years it takes for output per worker to double.
items.answer: 11.7 years

items.stem: Potential GDP in Selmaria is $1000 billion and grows at 2% a year. Supply-side reforms are expected to raise this to 3% a year. Calculate potential GDP after 15 years with and without the reforms, and assess two reasons why the reforms may not achieve this.
items.answer: Without: $1345.9 billion; with: $1558 billion (a gain of $212.1 billion). Reasons: long time lags, uncertain effect of tax incentives, poor implementation, weak demand so capacity unused, crowding out of finance.
items.markingKey: Compound growth each case [2]; difference [1]; two reasons with evaluation [2].

items.stem: Extract: In Valdoria, unemployment is 6.5%, inflation 4.0%, public debt 110% of GDP and the central bank policy rate 2.0%. Productivity growth has been below 1% a year for a decade. (a) Calculate the real policy interest rate. (b) Explain how monetary policy could be used and one limitation.
items.answer: (a) -2% (b) Raise rates to reduce inflation; lags and effect on growth.

items.stem: The government of Westaria deregulates the electricity supply industry. Explain how this could increase aggregate supply.
items.answer: Lower barriers to entry increase competition, reducing X-inefficiency and costs, encouraging innovation; LRAS shifts right.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: competition/efficiency; 1 mark: LRAS shift [2]

items.stem: Extract: In Selmaria, unemployment is 8.5%, inflation 1.0%, public debt 95% of GDP and the central bank policy rate 0.5%. Productivity growth has been below 1% a year for a decade. (a) Calculate the real policy interest rate. (b) Discuss the most appropriate policy mix for this economy.
items.answer: (a) -0.5% (b) Diagnosis of main problem; combination of demand and supply-side policies; trade-offs; justified judgement.

items.stem: The policy mix refers to
options: the share of public and private ownership
the mix of goods in the CPI
the mix of imports and exports
the combination of fiscal, monetary and supply-side policies used to achieve objectives
items.answer: the combination of fiscal, monetary and supply-side policies used to achieve objectives
items.markingKey: Policies can complement or offset each other.

items.stem: Explain why a mix of policies is usually more effective than relying on one policy.
items.answer: Different policies target different causes (demand-side for cyclical problems, supply-side for structural); combining them reduces conflicts and side-effects and allows faster and longer-lasting results.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: different causes; 1 mark: offset side-effects [2]

items.stem: Explain how a depreciation of the currency could be combined with fiscal policy to correct a current account deficit without causing a recession.
items.answer: Depreciation switches expenditure towards domestic goods (raising AD); a modest fiscal tightening reduces domestic absorption, freeing capacity for exports and limiting inflation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: expenditure switching; 1 mark: expenditure reducing balances AD [2]

items.stem: Calvania is experiencing steady growth but a structural budget deficit of 6% of GDP and rising debt. Analyse an appropriate mix of fiscal, monetary and supply-side policies for this economy.
items.answer: Gradual fiscal consolidation offset by lower interest rates; supply-side reforms to raise trend growth; avoid sharp austerity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: diagnosis; 1 mark each for appropriate fiscal, monetary and supply-side elements linked to the problem (max 3); 1 mark: recognition of trade-off or limitation [5]

items.stem: Calvania is experiencing a recession with unemployment at 9%, inflation at 0.5% and interest rates at 0.25%. Analyse an appropriate mix of fiscal, monetary and supply-side policies for this economy.
items.answer: Fiscal stimulus (infrastructure), QE and forward guidance; supply-side training for long-term unemployed; watch the budget deficit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: diagnosis; 1 mark each for appropriate fiscal, monetary and supply-side elements linked to the problem (max 3); 1 mark: recognition of trade-off or limitation [5]

items.stem: Zentara faces rising inflation, high unemployment in some regions and a widening trade deficit. (a) Explain what is meant by the policy mix. (b) ‘A government can achieve all its macroeconomic objectives with the right policy mix.’ Evaluate this statement.
